_rules: Lane Reach copy. Headlines at most ten words. Body at most two sentences, forty words. Every number is a {{placeholder}} filled from /api at render time; the only digits typed here are story clocks and beat numbers.
disclaimer: Concept demo. Synthetic, calibrated data. Not affiliated with or endorsed by TEPCO or Mitsubishi Electric.
provenance: local controller, not the managed AlphaEvolve service

why.hero: Your price book is code, and code can evolve.
why.lede: Tokyo spot power averaged {{fy2025_mean}} JPY/kWh in FY2025, and the FY2026 scenarios the search is judged on run at {{fy2026_mean}} JPY/kWh. A book priced on last year's costs carries that gap as risk.

timeline.title: The price regime moved. The book did not.

frozen.title: Before the search starts, the judge is chosen
lines: The holdout of {{cohort}} customers and {{scenarios_holdout}} scenarios is generated and its hash written down. Nobody evaluates anything on it until the run itself does.
The success rule is fixed in advance: keep every customer rule on those unseen customers and beat the seed there.

findings.label: unseen customers, generated after the rules were written
content hash, recorded before any evaluation

frozen.note: docs/PREREGISTRATION_tariff_v4.md, the design sections, written before holdout3 existed.
frozen.cue: Point at the hash. It is the promise that nothing was tuned afterwards.

first.title: The search starts from your book and edits it
lines: The seed is your cost-plus book, scored at {{seed_train}} JPY M on the train scenarios. The first edits arrive within minutes; some score, some fail, all are recorded.
Every candidate runs in a sealed box with no network and no disk, and returns only its pricing decisions.
first.note: Scores are on the train fold: search progress, never uplift.
first.cue: Read the seed score aloud. Everything is measured against it.

caught.title: A candidate scores well by pricing customers out
lines: Candidate {{caught_id}} would have scored {{caught_raw}} JPY M, better than the seed. It got there by pushing churn past the rule in two segments.
The rule rejected it before the score could count, so it never entered the population.
caught.note: Pricing customers out is a strategy change, not an uplift.
caught.cue: This is the beat that makes the rules real. Let the insight text sit.

champion.title: {{programs_in_run}} candidates later, one book leads on train
lines: Candidate {{champion_id}} scores {{champion_train}} JPY M on train, {{champion_gain_train}} JPY M better than the seed. That is search progress, not a result, because these are the scenarios it was tuned on.
It moves fixed-price risk onto a market-linked share, sets margins by segment, and shares demand-response value with flexible customers.

findings.label: better than the seed on train, not citable
from the seed to the champion

champion.note: The champion is chosen on train. The holdout is only reported, so it cannot be gamed.
champion.cue: Say 'not a result' out loud. The next beat is the result.

holdout.title: The top five meet the customers they never saw
lines: The five best train candidates are scored once on the {{cohort}} holdout customers and their harsher scenario bank. The seed scores {{holdout_seed}} JPY M there; the champion {{champion_holdout}} JPY M.
The uplift a person may cite is the difference, and it carries a caveat you will see next.
holdout.note: Scale: the holdout scores are about three times the train scores because the cohort is three times larger.
holdout.cue: Pause on the delta. Then say: and here is what it depends on.

caveat.title: One small segment passes only with the margin
lines: In the {{fab_n}}-customer semiconductor segment, churn rises {{fab_rise_pp}} points. The point rule allows {{fab_point_pp}}; the pre-registered margin for a segment that small allows {{fab_margin_pp}}.
Under the old point rules, ranks {{rank_invalid_v3}} of the top five would be invalid. Ranks {{rank_both}} pass both rule sets, with a smaller uplift.

findings.label: ranks that pass both rule sets

caveat.note: The caveat travels with the number: in the tables, in the analyst's answers, and on every screen here.
caveat.cue: Do not rush this. The caveat is the credibility of the whole demo.

analyst.title: Ask the analyst whether every rule held
lines: The Lab Analyst reads the same tables and answers with citations. Watch it choose its tools and reach the caveat on its own.
If the model call fails, the page says so and replays a recorded answer, labelled as a replay.
analyst.question: {{analyst_question}}
analyst.note: One live question through the same stream the workspace uses.
analyst.cue: Let it run. Read the tool names as they light.

contrast.title: Three hand-tuned runs, then one pre-registered run
lines: On the left, the way it went before: three runs, each with a champion that broke a customer rule on unseen customers, and two holdouts burned for diagnosis.
On the right, the run whose rules were frozen first.

after_rows.text: Holdout of {{cohort}} customers generated after the rules were written; hash recorded.
{{policy_caught_run}} candidates rejected by the churn rule before scoring.
Champion {{champion_id}} judged once on unseen customers.
Uplift with its caveat, in the tables and in every answer.
A person marks the block read. Nothing promotes it.

contrast.note: Every earlier run is kept in the evidence; none was modified.
contrast.cue: Point left, then right. The difference is the order of events.

options.title: The rules strike the best-paying candidate
lines: Three candidates from the same run. The one that pays most on paper got there by pricing customers out, and the rules struck it before anyone had to argue.
The other two are valid; one needs the margin, one does not.
options.note: Selection is on train. The holdout figures are reported, never used to choose.
options.cue: Point at the struck card, then at the reason.

decide.title: Mark it read. Nothing here promotes it.
lines: What the run could not settle comes first, then the analyst's case. The hold records that a person read the evolved block, and nothing more.
Promotion needs a run on the managed service and stays disabled here.

hold.label: Hold to mark human-reviewed
hold.note: Read the evolved block on the alpha story screen

decide.note: The hold posts to the same review endpoint the workspace uses; the record lands in runs/reviews.jsonl.
decide.cue: Hold with the mouse. They must see you decide, and see what the button cannot do.

map.title: Where the value landed, on unseen customers
lines: Four readings from the holdout, seed against champion. The first is the citable one and carries its caveat; the rest explain where it comes from.
Most of the gain is tail risk removed, not margin per customer.
map.note: Every tile reads the run's evidence file.
map.cue: End on the caveat. It is what makes the number believable.

who.hero: Four roles, before and after, with their agents
who.lede: The people who own the book, the desk, the battery and the governance. Pick one to see what changes.

pricing_lead.jtbd: Renew the book so it holds margin under FY2026 prices without pricing any segment out.
pricing_lead.today: A cost-plus renewal book tuned on last year's costs, defended in front of the risk committee with a back-test on the same data it was tuned on.
pricing_lead.after: The search proposes books, the churn rule rejects any that price a segment out, and unseen customers judge the rest. The number you quote carries its caveat.

trading_head.jtbd: Lower the cost to serve the balance group while staying inside the plan-based band in every half-hour.
trading_head.today: Rule-based bidding tuned on last year's prices, with an imbalance temptation that no back-test punishes.
trading_head.after: Strategies that lean on the imbalance price are rejected before scoring. Held-out days decide what counts, and every catch is on the record.

bess_owner.jtbd: Prove the battery's contribution on days it never saw, inside warranty, in a figure the customer can audit.
bess_owner.today: A dispatch policy defended with a vendor back-test, and a gain-share the customer cannot check.
bess_owner.after: Every validated run shows seed against champion on held-out days, with cycles per day next to the warranty line.

ai_governance.jtbd: Let an evolved program near production only when the evidence and a named reviewer say so.
ai_governance.today: Model output arrives as a recommendation with no audit trail, and nobody can say what it could not do.
ai_governance.after: Nothing promotes code here. A two-second hold records a review; the gate lists what stays open, and every run says which controller produced it.

team.hero: Five agents, one loop, one place a person signs
team.lede: The lead proposes, the specialists test and judge, the reviewer strikes, and the analyst explains. Open any of them.

tiers.name: The lead
tiers.desc: Proposes edits to your book and keeps the search inside its budget.

tiers.name: Specialists, working together
tiers.desc: Score every candidate in a sealed box, then judge the best on unseen customers.

tiers.name: The reviewer
tiers.desc: Strikes any candidate that breaks a customer or market rule, before it can score.

tiers.name: The analyst you can ask
tiers.desc: Reads the tables and answers with citations, live.

controller.name: The controller
controller.title: Proposes the next edit to your book
controller.desc: Picks a parent and two inspirations, asks a model for a code edit, and hands it to the sandbox.
controller.problem: Tuning a book by hand is slow, unrepeatable, and the rules that made it live in someone's head.
controller.stake: Every proposal is a diff against your seed, kept with its rationale.

evaluator.name: The evaluator
evaluator.title: Scores every candidate on the same market
evaluator.desc: Settles each candidate's decisions against the market model, the customer book and the battery fleet.
evaluator.problem: A back-test on the data a rule was tuned on proves nothing; scores must come from one trusted simulator.
evaluator.stake: Same customers, same scenarios, same score for everyone.

rows.v: the score, and what a candidate would have scored before the rules
it cannot change the rules or the data; the instance hash is checked after every run

flow.biz: Only decisions cross the boundary.
The same book every time.

flow.v: none: a score is not a decision
flow.biz: The rules judge next.
Never overwritten.

invariants.name: The rules
invariants.title: Strikes what cheats before it can count
invariants.desc: Churn, fair pricing, essential facilities, non-discrimination, intentional imbalance, battery limits.
invariants.problem: A search will find the imbalance loophole and the segment to price out. Something has to say no before the score counts.
invariants.stake: A struck candidate never enters the population, whatever it would have scored.

rows.v: the settled decisions of every candidate
valid or struck, with the reason in plain words
it cannot soften a rule after the fact; the judgment rules were pre-registered

flow.biz: Every candidate, no exceptions.

flow.v: churn by segment, imbalance by slot, prices vs reference
flow.biz: The same rules the risk committee reads.
The reason is kept with the score it would have had.

flow.v: none: a strike is final for the run
flow.biz: No appeal inside the search.
Every catch is on the record.

invariants.ask: Which invariants rejected candidates in the latest tariff run, and what would they have scored?

holdout_judge.name: The holdout judge
holdout_judge.title: Judges the best on customers they never saw
holdout_judge.desc: Scores the top five train candidates once on a fresh cohort and a harsher scenario bank.
holdout_judge.problem: A champion chosen and judged on the same data is a back-test, not a result.
holdout_judge.stake: The holdout is reported, never used to choose, so it cannot be gamed.

rows.v: the holdout cohort and bank, the seed on the same cohort
valid or not on unseen customers, and the delta a person may cite
one judgment per cohort; a cohort used for diagnosis is burned

flow.biz: Only then does the holdout open.
Data the search never saw.

flow.v: holdout delta, with the sampling-margin caveat
flow.biz: The only number an uplift may cite.
A delta is evidence, not a decision.
The caveat is a column, not a footnote.

built.hero: Nothing here promotes code to production

built.boundary_sub: The search writes evidence files and the analyst reads tables. The only write a person can trigger is a review record, and the promotion control stays disabled for every local run.
